turns.question: So what can you help me with?

response.answer:
The CDC can help you with finding and approving internships, understanding Approved Experience course requirements, exploring the optional paid CO-OP program, and participating in IAESTE international internship exchanges.

For career readiness and professional development, you can access:
- CV and cover letter guidelines, as well as online modules covering resume writing, interview preparation, job search, and workplace skills.
- One-to-one consultations for resume reviews, mock interviews, and career counseling.
- Career+, an initiative for career planning and certification available at https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/CareerPlus.aspx.
- MentorPlus+ to connect with AUB alumni for career guidance.
- Full-time job vacancies shared via email and the AUB Career Portal.

You can find summer internship listings, letter requests, and self-secured internship forms on the CDC students page at https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/students.aspx.

history.content: So what can you help me with?

- Career+, an initiative for career planning and certification available at https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/CareerPlus.aspx.
- MentorPlus+ to connect with AUB alumni for career guidance.
- Full-time job vacancies shared via email and the AUB Career Portal.

You can find summer internship listings, letter requests, and self-secured internship forms on the CDC students page at https://www.aub.edu.lb/msfea/cdc/Pages/students.aspx.

response.answer:
The Approved Experience internship is a graduation requirement normally completed during the summer before your final year. It allows you to apply academic learning to practical technical challenges, develop workplace skills, and explore career paths. Registration requires at least 90 credits. The standard requirement is a minimum of eight full weeks of approved, discipline-related technical training (typically 320 work hours) in Lebanon or abroad. The course is graded Pass or Fail.

The ordinary process moves through three major stages:
- Before training: You secure an internship independently or through Career Development Center postings, obtain formal placement approval, and submit your proposal.
- During training: You confirm your arrival, complete the professional skills lectures and quiz, and submit a mid-experience progress report.
- At completion: You submit your final training report, final presentation, required evaluation and summary forms, and official employer completion documentation.

To check placement eligibility or clarify any specific course arrangements, you can contact the course contact, Rafika Dinnawi, at rd39@aub.edu.lb.

response.answer:
CO-OP is an optional program that allows you to combine your studies with a paid, full-time work placement (35–40 hours per week) lasting at least 6 months. Placements typically span Summer and Fall or Spring and Summer during your 3rd or 4th year, and passing the co-op replaces your department's Approved Experience requirement.

The typical process involves:
- Preparation and application: Attend advising sessions, complete career development modules, and apply to the program for departmental review.
- Placement: Pursue program opportunities or submit a self-found opportunity using the Proposal of Cooperative Education and Experiential Learning Form for advisor approval.
- Work term and registration: Maintain full-time status by registering for FEAA 500 in the first semester and FEAA 500A in the second semester, complete the work term with employer evaluations and a midterm site visit, and return to campus for at least one term before graduating.

For next steps, consult the MSFEA CO-OP Handbook or reach out to the CO-OP CDC Advisor.
